summary: Bootstrap criteria-fit fails closed. Package separation, exact ADR-018 emission, bounded repair, and read-only authority remain intact, and production environment mocks are no longer selectable. Blocking gaps remain in Pi attestation order and cross-process re-verification, runtime-parent and prompt containment, cleanup coverage, and proof that the router-selected model overrides remaining static defaults.

acceptance_criteria_status.criterion: The harness is physically separate from packages/worker-harness and never loads craft-pool.
evidence: packages/orchestrator-harness/package.json exposes only package-local agents and skills.
test/work-intake/decomposition-architecture-boundaries.test.ts checks package separation and absence of worker-harness/craft-pool dependencies.
.tmp/crafts-output/orchestrator-decomposition-harness-attempt-2/green-full.txt reports the architecture regressions passing.

acceptance_criteria_status.criterion: Its decomposer emits only id, intent, change_spec, acceptance_criteria, and depends_on for each node.
evidence: src/domains/work-intake/decomposition-harness.ts validateCandidate() admits exactly the five ADR-018 node fields and rejects unknown fields.
packages/orchestrator-harness/contracts/decomposition-emission.schema.json is checked by test/work-intake/decomposition-harness.test.ts for validator equivalence.
.tmp/crafts-output/orchestrator-decomposition-harness-attempt-2/green-work-intake.txt reports exact-shape and unknown-field tests passing.

acceptance_criteria_status.criterion: Kimi K3 is the bootstrap decomposition model with only approved fail-closed fallback policy.
evidence: packages/orchestrator-harness/config/model-routing.bootstrap.json correctly declares moonshot/kimi-k3 primary and openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol as the sole fallback.
packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/pi-model-invoker.mjs places the selected provider-qualified ID after --model, and direct fake-launcher tests cover both IDs.

packages/orchestrator-harness/config/settings.json still declares subagents.defaultModel as moonshot/kimi-k3, while no real Pi 0.81.1 test or effective-model attestation proves that the CLI selector overrides this subagent default for the Sol path.

packages/orchestrator-harness/test/launch.test.mjs exercises Sol-only availability only through preflight and does not assert successful end-to-end decomposition, effective model identity, or fallback provenance.

acceptance_criteria_status.criterion: The invocation records prompt, model, tool, package, and code-graph revision provenance.
evidence: src/domains/work-intake/decomposition-harness.ts constructs immutable records containing sanitized prompt, selected model, routing, breadth tool, package, Pi executable identity, policies, and index revision.
packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/run-decomposition.mjs supplies Pi path/version/digest to runDecomposition.

packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/pi-identity.mjs executes the candidate Pi file for --version before its digest is checked against the pinned digest, and run-decomposition.mjs executes --list-models before re-verification.

run-decomposition.mjs accepts a newly observed digest as its invocation baseline without comparing it to config/runtime-versions.json, so replacement after preflight can execute and be recorded as though it were the trusted Pi identity.

acceptance_criteria_status.criterion: Schema-invalid output is rejected or repaired only within an explicit bounded policy; the model cannot validate, persist, approve, or dispatch its own DAG.
evidence: src/domains/work-intake/decomposition-harness.ts enforces strict output shape, byte/node/collection limits, one schema-only repair, and an invocation-wide deadline.
packages/orchestrator-harness/agents/spec-decomposer.md restricts tools to read and forbids validation, persistence, approval, queue, Gate 1, and dispatch authority.
.tmp/crafts-output/orchestrator-decomposition-harness-attempt-2/green-full.txt reports repair-bound, timeout, shape, and authority tests passing.

risks: After correct digest-before-execution verification, a narrow operating-system time-of-check/time-of-use interval will remain between final verification and spawn.
Uncatchable process termination can still leave a private runtime subtree behind.
Previously accepted residual risks remain: deterministic secret recognition may miss novel encodings, and provider cancellation may lag the local timeout.
recommended_next_step: Return to F. Verify the pinned Pi digest before any version or registry execution and on every later spawn; carry the pinned identity across preflight rather than re-baselining it; use a trusted canonical runtime base with canonical ownership/mode/ancestry checks; enforce prompt containment against symlink races; cover controlled cleanup outcomes; and remove or conclusively neutralize subagents.defaultModel with an effective Pi-model test.

attempted: Reviewed the five original criteria, attempt-2 C and revised C, passed plan-security constraints, R artifact, attempt-1 final T findings, changed production sources, focused tests, and persisted green/red verification output.

Audited production mock removal, model argv and fallback composition, static settings, trusted interpreter and PATH handling, runtime-parent and prompt containment, cleanup ownership, Pi identity provenance, and re-verification.
Audited the test suite against the revised plan rather than treating passing tests as sufficient.
failure_context.failure_reason: The active process boundary can execute changed Pi bytes before pinned-digest validation, private runtime containment is not established against caller-controlled temporary roots or symlink races, cleanup coverage is incomplete, and effective Sol selection remains unproven while a static Kimi default remains.
discoveries: Production scripts no longer consume AGENT_POOL_TEST_MODE, AGENT_POOL_MOCK_*, or AGENT_POOL_TEST_RECORD_PATH; launch.mjs rejects them.
All Pi subprocess call sites use process.execPath and a fixed /usr/bin:/bin PATH rather than caller PATH.
The focused suite's launch cleanup assertion checks the workspace .agent-pool path, not the actual runtime subtree created under the temporary base.
dead_ends: This read-only evaluator had no command-execution tool, so persisted test outputs were reviewed but not rerun.
No runtime evidence was provided showing Pi 0.81.1's effective selected model when --model conflicts with subagents.defaultModel.

criteria_fit.rationale: Three criteria have direct passing evidence, but the model-routing and provenance criteria lack complete trustworthy evidence and have blocking implementation mismatches. The bootstrap hard gate therefore fails closed.

correctness_risk.rationale: Major boundary defects allow changed Pi bytes to run before pinned-digest validation and permit re-baselining after preflight; runtime containment also remains raceable.

locality_simplicity.rationale: The implementation is split into focused helpers, but identity verification, registry invocation, environment construction, containment, and cleanup are inconsistently composed across several scripts.

interface_clarity.rationale: The selected-model and Pi-identity interfaces are narrow, but optional identity fallback, duplicated launcher/piExecutable provenance, and a remaining static default obscure which values are authoritative.

type_error_safety.rationale: JavaScript process-boundary checks rely on lexical prefix tests, omit canonical ownership/mode checks for derived roots, execute before attestation, and lack complete child spawn/signal cleanup handling.

test_quality.rationale: The suite is broad but misses the revised C's critical adversarial cases: digest-before-execution, replacement between preflight and run-decomposition, hostile temporary roots and prompt symlink races, controlled cleanup failures, repair-call model argv, and effective Pi model selection. One launch cleanup test asserts an unrelated workspace path.

blocking_findings.message: Pi bytes are executed before pinned identity is established, and the post-preflight process re-baselines an unpinned replacement.
evidence: packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/pi-identity.mjs verifyPiIdentity() runs the candidate file with --version before hashing it or comparing it with the configured digest.
packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/preflight.mjs compares runtime.launcherDigest only after verifyPiIdentity() has executed the candidate.

packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/run-decomposition.mjs runs launcherPath --list-models before calling verifyPiIdentity(), then accepts the newly observed digest without comparing it to config/runtime-versions.json.

packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/pi-model-invoker.mjs calls verifyPiIdentity() before comparing the returned digest with the earlier identity, so replaced bytes can execute during the purported pre-spawn check.

packages/orchestrator-harness/test/pi-model-invoker.test.mjs checks rejection after replacement but does not assert that the replacement writes no marker during --version execution or cover replacement between preflight and run-decomposition.

blocking_findings.message: The private runtime and prompt containment boundary remains caller-influenced and symlink-raceable.
evidence: packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/runtime-parent.mjs derives RUNTIME_BASE from node:os tmpdir(), which honors inherited temporary-directory environment variables, despite revised C excluding ambient temporary roots.
runtime-parent.mjs does not validate the base's ownership, mode, canonical non-symlink ancestry, or return a canonical parent path.

packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/preflight.mjs uses lexical startsWith(runtimeParent) checks for HOME/XDG without a path separator and does not validate their ownership, mode, canonical containment, or symlink ancestry.

packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/pi-model-invoker.mjs recursively creates runtimeParent/prompts and uses lexical joined paths without revalidating the parent, prompt directory, or prompt file against symlink replacement.

packages/orchestrator-harness/test/runtime-parent.test.mjs and pi-model-invoker.test.mjs cover ordinary paths only; they do not cover hostile TMPDIR, prefix-collision paths, ancestor symlinks, or prompt-directory replacement.

blocking_findings.message: Whole-subtree cleanup is not guaranteed for all controlled launcher outcomes, and the integration assertion does not inspect the actual runtime subtree.
evidence: packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/launch.mjs cleans after preflight failure and child exit only; it has no child error handler or controlled SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup path.
packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/runtime-parent.mjs silently abandons cleanup if the recorded parent cannot be realpathed, including replacement or rename races.
packages/orchestrator-harness/test/launch.test.mjs 'launch cleans the runtime subtree' checks workspace/.agent-pool, although runtime-parent.mjs creates the subtree under its temporary runtime base.
The revised C test strategy required success, validation failure, spawn failure, timeout, abort, repair, and cleanup-error coverage, but the focused suite reports no such launcher-level matrix.

blocking_findings.message: Exact effective model selection is not demonstrated while a static Kimi default remains active.
evidence: packages/orchestrator-harness/config/settings.json still sets subagents.defaultModel to moonshot/kimi-k3.

packages/orchestrator-harness/scripts/pi-model-invoker.mjs correctly emits --model as a separate argv pair, but packages/orchestrator-harness/test/pi-model-invoker.test.mjs uses a fake script that only captures argv and cannot prove Pi 0.81.1 or pi-subagents honors that selector over subagents.defaultModel.
packages/orchestrator-harness/test/launch.test.mjs proves Sol-only preflight acceptance but does not assert successful decomposition, routing provenance, or effective Sol identity.

If Pi's global --model is contractually authoritative over the subagent default, retaining defaultModel may be harmless; however, no pinned-runtime attestation or documented invariant establishes that tradeoff, and the revised plan explicitly required static defaults to be removed or neutralized.
